source_review.notes: Checked twelve current primary documentation sources from Apache Spark, Apache Flink, Trino, Dask, and Apache Beam. All URLs returned HTTP 200. Sources support associative/commutative combine requirements, local mapper combination, accumulator types, one/two-stage aggregation, hash/spill behavior, SQL null and ordered aggregates, distinct strategies, recursive group aggregation, and combine transforms.

evidence: Reviewed input/state/output domains V/S/O, fresh zero, add, merge, finalize, input/partial counts N/C, sizes v/s, variance state (n,mean,M2), and aggregate generation.
Checked associativity, commutativity, identity, idempotence, exactness, boundedness, order sensitivity, and determinism remain distinct properties.
Checked group key, snapshot, function/state schema version, partition, tree/subtree, producer, spill, accepted attempt, and final commit identities are consistent.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Internal accumulator identity is separated from user-visible empty/null results and from physical execution.

evidence: Executed distributed-aggregation-states with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced eight inputs, five partial states, and three final groups.
Reproduced a=(sum 60,count 3,nulls 1,mean 20), b=(45,3,0,15), c=(0,0,1,null), and 37.5% record-count reduction.
Recomputed partial-mean counterexample as correct mean 900/10=90 versus unweighted mean-of-means 50.
Recomputed exercise bytes as 640,000,000 input and 38,400,000 partial, ratio 0.06 and 94% reduction.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture validates state sufficiency, identity freshness, component merge, null accounting, and record counts only; it is not a distributed, byte-size, spill, numeric-stability, or performance benchmark.

evidence: Verified induction over the aggregation tree from exact leaf states, associative merge, commutativity when reordered, identity, and exact accepted leaf coverage.
Verified mean state merges componentwise and finalizes once, unlike unweighted partial means.
Reviewed parallel variance merge n=n_a+n_b, mean update, and M2 cross term including empty/singleton cases.
Verified shuffled-byte ratio Cs/(Nv) and separated it from record ratio and physical overhead.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The algebraic proof does not establish bounded state, floating-point bitwise reproducibility, or performance.

evidence: Reviewed empty/global/grouped inputs, all-null values, null keys, duplicates, filters, distinct, grouping sets, one/all groups, high cardinality, hot groups, and giant states.
Reviewed integer/decimal overflow, negative/zero weights, floating cancellation, subnormals, infinities, NaNs, signed zero, comparator ties, and order-sensitive aggregates.
Reviewed hash collision/skew, recursive spill, disk full, corrupt/truncated state, worker loss, retry, speculation, cancellation, mixed versions, adaptive trees, and sink failures.
Reviewed approximate error/seed compatibility, connector/metadata pushdown mismatch, sensitive state leakage, auth/region/tenant limits, holds, and deletion.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Algebra, SQL semantics, numerical behavior, resource boundedness, attempt coverage, approximation, and governance can fail independently.

evidence: Traced each logical input through fresh local state, optional spill/intermediate tree, compatible serialization, one accepted contribution, complete final group, finalize, and one committed output.
Checked group normalization/equality/partitioning and accumulator schema/code/semantics remain pinned across all stages.
Checked null/empty/filter/distinct/order/overflow/approximation semantics survive partialization and finalization.
Checked hash/sort state, spill, tree fan-in, network, output, concurrent tasks, recovery, and cleanup are charged and bounded.
invariant_checking.notes: Content equality cannot replace attempt identity because distinct producers may legitimately emit equal non-idempotent states.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from result semantics and state definition through algebra, costing, physical tree, admission, accepted partials, finalize/commit, validation, and deletion.
Checked decomposable-aggregate proof by induction over arbitrary partition and merge trees.
Checked counterexamples for average-of-averages, shared mutable zero, associativity-versus-commutativity, commutativity-versus-retry safety, partial median insufficiency, and floating reassociation.
Checked distinct, ordered, holistic, approximate, pushdown, metadata, and hot-key cases retain additional premises.
proof_review.notes: Correctness requires sufficient compatible states and exact accepted input coverage; economic benefit remains empirical.

evidence: Audited uses of associative, commutative, idempotent, exact, approximate, sufficient, bounded, deterministic, compatible, accepted, and complete.
Confirmed floating-point, sketch error, metadata correctness, and connector pushdown claims state their limits.
Confirmed current Spark/Flink/Trino/Dask/Beam behaviors are sourced and not presented as universal runtime guarantees.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Semantic laws, numerical approximations, planner heuristics, and operational evidence are clearly separated.

evidence: Reviewed proposed measurements for rows/bytes, groups/states, reduction, state tails, hash/sort/spill, tree depth/fan-in, shuffle, hot keys, CPU, output, numerical warnings, retries, and cleanup.
Confirmed no universal combine depth, partition count, hash load, spill threshold, sketch precision, salt count, pushdown policy, tolerance, or retention is prescribed.
Checked record versus byte reduction, logical versus physical bytes, exact versus approximate, mean versus tail, and accepted versus losing attempts remain separate.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production decisions require representative cardinality/repetition/state/output distributions, numeric requirements, runtime/storage/topology, connector semantics, threats, and policy evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distributed aggregation as a mergeable accumulator algebra plus physical local/intermediate/final execution, spanning common and complex states, hash/sort organization, reduction economics, null/empty/order/numeric semantics, distinct/sketches, retries, pushdown, security, and lifecycle.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical accumulator APIs, fresh ownership, map-side combine, tree aggregation, spill, partitioning, high cardinality/hot keys, UDAF versioning, connector evidence, metrics, fault injection, accepted attempts, and governed deletion. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from algebra and sufficient state through standard aggregates, physical execution, scale, failure, validation, and governance. Ten examples and five complete exercises cover mean weighting, byte reduction, high cardinality, attempts, distinct state, ordered aggregates, empty semantics, trees, versions, variance, classification, and sensitive distinct counting.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark, Flink, Trino, Dask, or Beam maintainer, database/distributed-algorithms or numerical-analysis researcher, sketch/privacy specialist, runtime/storage/network/performance specialist, connector owner, security/privacy/legal/records authority, affected-tenant reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
